1.1: *"And Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him" (Genesis 5:24).*
1.2: Rabbi Ishmael said: When I ascended to the heights to behold the vision of the Chariot, I entered into six palaces, chamber within chamber. When I reached the entrance of the seventh palace, I stood in prayer before the Holy One, blessed be He, and I lifted my eyes toward the heights and said: "Master of the Universe, I beseech You, grant me at this hour the merit of Aaron the son of Amram, who loved peace and pursued peace, and who received the crown of priesthood from before Your Glory at Mount Sinai, so that Qatspiel the Prince and the angels with him do not prevail over me, and let them not cast me down from heaven."
1.3: Immediately, the Holy One, blessed be He, summoned Metatron, His servant, the angel and Prince of the Presence; he flew on his wings and came out to meet me with great joy to save me from their hands. He grasped me by my hand before their eyes and said to me: "Enter in peace, for you have found favor before the Master of the Universe to behold the likeness of the Chariot." At that time, I entered the seventh palace, and he guided me to the camp of the Shekhinah and stood me before the Throne of Glory to behold the Chariot.
1.4: And when my eyes beheld the princes of the Chariot and the princes of the flame, they set their eyes upon me. Immediately I recoiled and trembled, and I fell backward and was stunned by the radiance of the likeness of their eyes and the splendor of the appearance of their faces, until the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked them and said to them: "My servants, Seraphim, Cherubim, and Ophannim, hide your eyes from Ishmael, My son, My beloved, My darling, and My glory, so that he may not recoil and tremble."
1.5: Immediately, Metatron, the Prince of the Presence, came and restored my soul and stood me upon my feet. Yet I still did not have the strength to utter a song before the Throne of Glory of the King of Glory, the Mightiest of all kings, the Radiance of all nobles, until hour after hour had passed. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, opened for me the gates of the Shekhinah: the gates of peace, the gates of wisdom, the gates of power, the gates of might, the gates of speech, the gates of song, the gates of holiness, and the gates of melody. He enlightened my eyes and my heart with the recitation of praise and laudation, joy and thanksgiving, melody, beauty and majesty, praise, etc. I yearned for His presence and offered a song before the Throne of Glory. The Holy Creatures beneath the Throne of the King of Glory and those above the Throne answered after me and said: "Holy," and "Blessed is the glory of the LORD from His place."

2.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: At that time At that hour, the bearers of the Chariot, the wheels of flame, and the wheels of consuming fire were asking Metatron, and they were saying to him: "Youth, for what reason did you allow a child of a woman to come and gaze upon the Chariot? From what nation is he? From what tribe is he? What is his nature?"
2.2: Metatron answered and said to them: "He is from the nation of Israel, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, chose to be His nation out of seventy languages. He is from the tribe of Levi—a heave-offering to His name. He is from the seed of Aaron, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, chose to be His minister, for the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself bound upon him the crown of priesthood at Sinai." Immediately they opened [their mouths] and said: "Surely he is worthy to gaze upon the Chariot, as it is written: 'Happy is the people for whom it is thus,' etc." (Psalm 144:15).

3.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: At that hour I asked Metatron, the Prince of the Presence; I said to him: "What is your name?" He said to me: "I have seventy names corresponding to the seventy languages in the world, and all of them are after the name of the [King of Kings], but my King calls me 'Youth'."

4.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: I said to Metatron: "For what reason are you called by the name of my Creator with seventy names, and you are greater than all the princes, higher than all the angels, more beloved than all the ministers, more honored than all the hosts, and greater than all the mighty ones in sovereignty, in greatness, and in glory—and yet, for what reason do they call you in the heights of heaven 'Youth'?"
4.2: He answered and said to me: "Because I am Enoch, the son of Jared. For when the children of the generation of the Flood sinned and acted corruptly in their deeds, and said to God, 'Depart from us,' etc., and said to God, 'Depart from us, for we do not desire the knowledge of Your ways' (Job 21:14), the Holy One, blessed be He, took me from among them to be a witness against them in the heights of heaven to all who come into the world. This was so that they should not say, 'The Merciful One is cruel; for what did all those multitudes sin—their wives, their sons, and their daughters, their horses, their mules, their cattle, and their possessions, and all the birds that were in the world—that the Holy One, blessed be He, destroyed them with [the sinners] in the days of the Flood?' What will the world say? 'If these, the generation of the Flood, sinned—the beasts, the animals, and the birds, what was their sin that they perished with them?' Therefore, the Holy One, blessed be He, raised me up in their lifetime before their eyes to the heights of heaven to be a witness against them for the world to come. And the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed me in the heights as a prince and a ruler among the ministering angels."
4.3: At that hour, three angels from among the ministering angels—'Uzzah, 'Azzah, and 'Aza'el—came and were bringing accusations against me in the heights of heaven, and they said before the Holy One, blessed be He: "Did not the former ones speak well before You … ?"
4.4: 'Do not create man.' Furthermore, the Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them: 'Even though I have made [him], I will bear, and I will carry, and I will deliver.' When they saw him, they said before Him: 'Lord of the Universe, what is the nature of this one who ascends to the highest heights? Is he not one of the seed of those who perished in the days of the Flood? What is his nature in the firmament?' Furthermore, the Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them: 'What is your business that you involve yourselves in My affairs? For I have desired this one more than all of you, that he should be a prince and a ruler over you in the heights of heaven.' Immediately, they all stood and went out to meet him and prostrated themselves before him, saying: 'Happy are you, and happy are your parents, for your Creator has desired you.' And because I am the smallest among them and a youth in my days—in days, months, and years—therefore they used to call me 'Youth.'

5.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: From the day that the Holy One, blessed be He, banished the first man (Adam) from the Garden of Eden, the Shekhinah dwelt upon a cherub beneath the Tree of Life. And the ministering angels were leaping and coming and descending in troop after troop from heaven, in company after company from the firmament, and in camp after camp from heaven, to do His will in the entire world. And the first man and his generation were sitting at the entrance of the Garden of Eden to look upon the likeness of the form of the radiance of the Shekhinah; for the radiance of the Shekhinah traveled from one end of the world to the other, [at a ratio of] one to sixty-five thousand of the solar orb. For anyone who gazed upon the radiance of that Shekhinah—flies and gnats would not light upon him, he would not fall ill, he would not suffer pain, and no damaging spirits could harm him. Moreover, even angels had no power over him. Whenever the Holy One, blessed be He, went out and entered into Eden, and from there to the Garden, and from the Garden to the firmament, and from the firmament to Eden, everyone would gaze upon the radiance of the likeness of His Shekhinah and were not harmed.
5.2: [This continued] until the members of the generation of Enosh the wicked arrived, who was the chief of all the idolaters in the world. And what did the members of his generation do? They would go from one end of the world to the other, and each and every one of them would bring silver and gold, precious stones and pearls, to high mountains and elevated hills, and they made them into idols in the four quarters of the world. They would station them in every quarter of the world upon a throne of a thousand a thousand parasangs. And they would bring down the sun, the moon, the stars, and the constellations, and set them before them, on their right and on their left, to serve them in the manner they used to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, [of whom it is said]: "And all the host of heaven stood by Him on His right hand and on His left." And how was there power within them that they could bring them down? It was because Uzza and Azzael—and Azzael was teaching them sorceries so that they would bring them down and make use of them; for were it not so, they would not have been able to bring them down.
5.3: In that hour, the ministering angels framed an accusation before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said before Him: "Lord of the Universe, what have You to do with the sons of man? As it is said: 'What is Enosh that You should remember him?' 'Adam' is not said here, but rather 'Enosh,' for he was the head of idolatry. Why have You left the highest heavens of heavens, the established place of the glory of Your name and the high and exalted throne in the heights of Arabot, and come to dwell with the sons of man who worship idols and have equated You with an idol? Now You are on the earth and idolatry is on the earth; what is Your nature among the dwellers of the earth, the worshippers of idols?"
5.4: Immediately, the Holy One, blessed be He, withdrew His Shekhinah from the earth, from among them. In that hour, the ministering angels and the divisions of the hosts and the armies of Arabot—a thousand camps and myriads of hosts—came and took trumpets and shofars in their hands and sounded the shofars. They surrounded the Shekhinah with songs, jubilation, and melodies, and He ascended to the heights of heaven, as it is said: "God has ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of the shofar."

6.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to bring me up to the height, He first sent Anaphiel YH the Prince to me, and he took me from among them before their eyes and mounted me in great glory upon a chariot of fire and horses of fire and servants of glory, and he brought me up with the Shekhinah to the heights of heaven.
6.2: And as soon as I arrived at the heights of heaven, the Holy Creatures (Hayyot HaKodesh), the Ophanim, the Seraphim, the Cherubim, the wheels of the Chariot (Merkabah), and the servants of consuming fire smelled my scent from a distance of three hundred and sixty-five thousand myriads of parasangs, and they said: "What is the scent of one born of woman, and what is the nature of a white drop, that it should ascend to the heights of heaven and serve among the hewers of flames?" The Holy One, blessed be He, answered and said to them: "My servants, Cherubim, Ophanim, and Seraphim, let it not be evil [in your eyes] … " to you regarding this matter: that all the sons of man denied Me and My great kingdom, and went and worshipped idols; so I withdrew My Shekhinah from among them and raised it to the height. And this one whom I took from among them is the chosen of them all, and he is equivalent to them all in faith and in righteousness and in the excellence of [his] deeds. And this one I asked as My reward in My world under all the heavens.

7.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me:  When the Holy One, blessed be He, took me from among the sons of the generation of the Flood, He raised me on the wings of the wind of the Shekhinah to the highest firmament and brought me into the great palaces in the heights of Arabot, the firmament, where the Throne of Glory of the Shekhinah is, along with the Chariot, and troops of fire, and troops and hosts of flame, and sharpeners of fire, and Cherubim of torches, and Ofannim of burning coals, and ministers of burning heat, and Hashmallim of lightning-flashes, and Seraphim of lightning-bolts. And He stationed me to serve the Throne of Glory every single day.

8.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Before He stationed me to serve the Throne of Glory, the Holy One, blessed be He, opened for me three hundred thousand gates of understanding, and three hundred thousand gates of prudence, and three hundred thousand gates of life, and three hundred thousand gates of peace, and three hundred thousand gates of the Shekhinah, and three hundred thousand gates of power and strength, and three hundred thousand gates of might, and three hundred thousand gates of grace and loving-kindness, and three hundred thousand gates of love, and three hundred thousand gates of Torah, and three hundred thousand gates of sustenance, and three hundred thousand gates of mercy, and three hundred thousand gates of humility, and three hundred thousand gates of the fear of heaven.
8.2: At that hour, the Holy One, blessed be He, added for me wisdom upon wisdom, understanding upon understanding, prudence upon prudence, knowledge upon knowledge, mercy upon mercy, Torah upon Torah, love upon love, loving-kindness upon loving-kindness, desire upon desire, humility upon humility, power upon power, might upon might, strength upon strength, splendor upon splendor, beauty upon beauty, form upon form. And I was honored and glorified with all good and praised qualities, more than all the dwellers of the heights. heights.

9.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me:  After all these measures, His hand was joined upon me and He blessed me with one thousand and three hundred and sixty-five thousand blessings. And I was uplifted and grew high as the measurement of the length and breadth of the seven heavens. And [I had] twenty-two thousand and six wings on one side, and thirty-six on the other; and every single wing was like the fullness of the world. And He fixed in me three hundred and sixty-five thousand eyes, and every single eye was like the great luminary. And He did not leave out any kind of radiance, nor any kind of splendor, form, beauty, or praise of lights in the world that He did not fix in me.

10.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: All this the Holy One, blessed be He, did for me: [He made] a throne similar to the Throne of Glory, and He spread over me a covering of radiance, of splendor, of form, of glory, of beauty, of grace, and of loving-kindness, similar to the covering of the Throne of Glory, in which all kinds of radiance of luminaries in the world are fixed. And He placed it at the entrance of the Seventh Palace and seated me upon it. And He caused a herald to proclaim concerning me in every single heaven, saying: "Metatron My servant, I have appointed him as prince and ruler over all the princes of My kingdom and over all the inhabitants of the heights, except for the eight great, honored, and awesome princes who are called 'Y-Y' by the name of the ruler, their King. And every single angel and every single prince who has a matter to speak before Me shall go before him and speak to him. And every single word that he speaks in My name to you, you shall observe and perform, because the Prince of Wisdom and the Prince of Understanding I have handed over to him, to teach him the wisdom of those above and those below, the wisdom of this world and the wisdom of the world to come. And I have also appointed him over all the treasuries of the Palace of Arabot and over all the storehouses of life that I have in the heights of heaven."

11.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: The Holy One, blessed be He, revealed to me then all the secrets of the Torah, and all the mysteries of wisdom, and all the depths of perfection. And all the thoughts of the hearts of creatures, and all the mysteries of the world, and all the orders of creation [Seder Bereshit] are revealed before me, just as they are revealed before the Creator of the Beginning. And I gazed intently to look into the deep mysteries and the wondrous glory; before a man thinks in secret, I see [it], and before a man does anything, I see [it], and there is nothing in the height and in the heaven of the world.

12.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Out of the love with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved me more than all the denizens of the heights, He gave me a garment of radiance in which all kinds of luminaries were fixed. He clothed me and made for me a robe of glory in which all kinds of splendor, radiance, luster, and majesty were fixed. He wrapped me and made for me a royal crown in which forty-nine stones of form were fixed, like the light of the sun’s orb, whose radiance goes forth to the four quarters of the Arabot firmament and the seven heavens, and to the four quarters of the world. He tied it upon my head and called me “the Lesser YHWH” before all His heavenly retinue in the heights, as it is said: "For My name is in him."

13.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: out of the great love and immense compassion with which the Holy One, blessed be He, loved me and cherished me more than all the denizens of the heights, He wrote with His finger, with a pen of flame, upon the crown that is on my head, the letters by which heaven and earth were created; the letters by which seas and rivers were created; the letters by which mountains and hills were created; the letters by which stars and constellations, lightnings, winds, and thunders, voices, snow and hail, tempest and storm were created; the letters by which all the needs of the world and all the orders of creation were created. And every single letter flashes from time to time like the appearance of lightnings, from time to time like the appearance of torches, from time to time like the appearance of the moon, from time to time like the appearance of the rising of the sun, moon, and stars.

14.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, tied this crown upon my head, all the princes of the kingdoms in the height of the Arabot firmament and all the hosts of every single firmament trembled because of it. Even the princes of the Elim, the princes of the Erelim, the princes of the Taphsarim, and the princes of the Erelim, who are greater than all the ministering angels who serve before the Throne of Glory, were shaken and quaked before me when they saw me. Even Samael, the prince of the accusers, who is greater than all the princes of the kingdoms in the heights, fears and trembles before me. And even the Angel of Fire, the Angel of Hail, the Angel of Wind, the Angel of Lightning, the Angel of the Meteor, the Angel of the Storm, the Angel of the Earthquake, and the Angel and the angel of snow, and the angel of rain, and the angel of the day, and the angel of the night, and the angel of the sun, and the angel of the moon, and the angel of the stars, and the angel of the constellations, who guide the world from time to time, and who nourish and sustain [it]. And they are terrified before me when they see me.
14.2: And these are the names of the princes who guide the world: Gabriel, the angel of fire; Bardiel, the angel of hail; Ruhiel, who is appointed over the wind; Baraqiel, who is appointed over the lightnings; Za'amiel, who is appointed over the wrath; Ziqiel, who is appointed over the sparks; Ra'ashiel, who is appointed over the earthquake; Ra'amiel, who is appointed over the thunder; Shalgiel, who is appointed over the snow; Matariel, who is appointed over the rain; Shimshiel, who is appointed over the day; Lailiel, who is appointed over the night; Galgaliel, who is appointed over the orb of the sun; Ofanniel, who is appointed over the wheels of the moon; Kokhaviel, who is appointed over the stars; and Rahtiel, who is appointed over the constellations. And all of them fall upon their faces when they see me, and they are unable to look at me because of the majesty and splendor, the beauty and the glory, the radiance of the light of the crown of glory that is upon my head.

15.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, the glory of the heights of all, said to me: When the Holy One, blessed be He, took me into the heavens to serve the Throne of Glory, and the wheels of the Merkavah, and all the needs of the Shekhinah, immediately my flesh was turned into flame, my sinews into flaming fire, my bones into coals of juniper, the light of my eyelids into the radiance of lightnings, the orbs of my eyes into torches of fire, the hair of my head into a blaze and a flame, all my limbs into wings of burning fire, and the bulk of my stature into a consuming fire. On my right were hewers of flames of fire, and on my left torches were burning, and around me blew a tempestuous wind and a storm, and the sound of a noise like a [great] noise was before me and behind me.

16.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, the glory of the heights of all, said to me: At first, I used to sit upon a great throne of glory at the entrance of the Seventh Palace, and I judged all the children of heights, the retinue of the Omnipresent. By the authority of the Holy One, blessed be He, He apportioned to him greatness and sovereignty, many [powers] and dominion, splendor and praise, a diadem and a crown, and glory over all the princes of kingdoms. When I sit in the Academy on High, and the princes of kingdoms stand over me from my right and from my left by the authority of the Holy One, blessed be He—and once it happened that one [Aher] came to gaze upon the vision of the Merkavah and fixed his eyes; for he gazed and trembled before me, and before the wings [that were] to go out from him, because of the fear of me, and the dread of me, and the awe of me. When he saw me, that I sit upon a throne like a king, and the ministering angels were standing over me like servants, and all the princes of kingdoms, bound with crowns, were surrounding me—at that hour he opened [his mouth] and spoke, saying: "Surely there are two powers in heaven!" Immediately a Divine Voice went forth from before the Shekhinah, saying: "Return, wayward children, except for Aher." For this reason, at that hour, came Anaphiel YHWH, the honored and glorious prince, crowned, wonderful, and awesome, in whose hand are the keys of the Holy One, blessed be He, and he struck me with sixty lashes of light and stood me upon my feet.

17.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, the glory of the heights of all, said to me: There are seven great princes, beautiful, awesome, wonderful, and honored, who are appointed over the seven heavens. And these are they: Michael, Gabriel, Shachqiel, Bardiel, Baraqiel, Kadqiel, and Sidriel. And all of them are princes of the host of the heavens, and with each one are four hundred and ninety-six thousand myriads of ministering angels. Michael, the great prince, is appointed over the seventh heaven, the highest, which is in Arabot. Gabriel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the sixth heaven, which is in Machon. Shachqiel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the fifth heaven, which is in Ma'on. Shachqiel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the fourth heaven, which is in Zebul. Kardiel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the third heaven, which is in Shehaqim. Baraqiel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the second heaven, which is in Rom Raqiya. Sidriel, the prince of the host, is appointed over the first heaven, which is in Vilon, in the heavens. Below them is Anali'el, the prince appointed over the orb of the sun, and with him are ninety-six and six great and honored angels who cause the orb of the sun to run in the firmament three hundred and sixty-five thousand parasangs each and every day.
17.2: Beneath them is Ophniel the Prince, who is appointed over the orb of the moon, and with him are eighty-eight angels who cause the orb of the moon to run three hundred and fifty-four thousand parasangs each and every night, whenever the moon stands in the east in its circuit. And when does it stand in the east in its circuit? One must say: at the time when it is born anew month by month. Beneath them is Rahtiel the Prince, who is appointed over the constellations, and with him are seventy-two great and honored angels. And why is his name called Rahtiel? Because he causes the constellations to run in their orbs and in their paths three hundred and thirty-nine thousand parasangs each and every night, from east to west and from west to east, because the orb returns there for the sun, the moon, the stars, and the constellations, which travel in it at night from west to east. Beneath them is Kokhaviel the Prince, who is appointed over all the stars, and with him are three hundred and sixty-five thousand myriads of ministering angels, noble and honored, who cause the stars to run from city to city and from province to province in the firmament of heaven. And above them are seventy-two princes of kingdoms on high, corresponding to the seventy languages in the world; and all of them are bound with royal crowns, and clothed in royal garments, and wrapped in royal ornaments, and all of them are mounted upon royal horses, and hold in their hands royal scepters.
17.3: And each and every one of them, when he travels in the firmament, royal attendants run before him with great honor and much glory, in the manner that they travel on earth with chariots and horsemen in great hosts, and with honor and greatness, praise, and laud, and beauty.

18.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, the glory of the heights of all, said to me: All the angels of the first firmament, when they see their prince, dismount from their horses and fall upon their faces. And the prince of the first firmament, when he sees [when he sees] the prince of the second firmament, he removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the second firmament, when he sees the prince of the third firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the third firmament, when he sees the prince of the fourth firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the fourth firmament, when he sees the prince of the fifth firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the fifth firmament, when he sees the prince of the sixth firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the sixth firmament, when he sees the prince of the seventh firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And the prince of the seventh firmament, when he sees the seventy-two princes of kingdoms, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face.
18.2: And the seventy-two princes of kingdoms, when they see the gatekeepers of the first palace which is in Arabot of the uppermost firmament, they remove the royal crown from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the first palace, when they see the gatekeepers of the second palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the second palace, when they see the gatekeepers of the third palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the third palace, when they see the gatekeepers of the fourth palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the fourth palace, when they [see] the gatekeepers of the fifth palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the fifth palace, when they see the gatekeepers of the sixth palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the sixth palace, when they see the gatekeepers of the seventh palace, remove the crown of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the gatekeepers of the seventh palace, when they see the four great and honored princes who are appointed The camps of the four camps of the Shekhinah remove the crowns of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces.
18.3: And the four great princes, when they see the Youth—who is tender and precious in the first rank at the head of all the celestial beings—remove the crowns of glory from atop their heads and fall upon their faces. And the Youth, who is tender and precious, when he sees Atriel, the great prince of three quarries in the height of Arabot of the uppermost firmament, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face.
18.4: And Atriel the great prince, when he sees Hamon, the great, awesome, and honored prince—who stands and is revered, who makes all the celestial beings tremble at the hour when the time is fixed to say "Holy," as he asks with the voice of a multitude [Hamon]: "Peoples are cut off from His loftiness, nations are shattered"—removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And Hamon the great prince, when he sees Tetrisiel Y. the prince, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And Tetrisiel Y. the great prince, when he sees Atruniel Y., removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face.
18.5: And Atruniel Y. the prince, when he sees Na'ariyuriel Y. the prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Na'ariyuriel Y. the prince, when he sees Sasnigal Y. the prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Sasnigal Y. the prince, when he sees Guriel Y. the prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Guriel Y. the prince, when he sees Gevurathiel Y. the prince, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face.
18.6: And Gevurathiel Y. the prince, when he sees Arphiel Y. the prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Arphiel Y. the prince, when he sees Ashriel Y. the prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Ashriel Y. the prince, head of every company of the celestial beings, when he sees Galitzur Y. the prince, who reveals secrets, would remove the crown of glory from atop [ … from] his head and falls upon his face. And Tsur Y. the Prince, when he sees Zekhophiel Y. the Prince—who is appointed to write the merits of Israel which they perform before the Throne of Glory—would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And Zekhophiel Y. the Prince, when he sees Anaphiel Y. the Prince—who guards the entrances of the palaces of Arabot of the firmament—would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Anaphiel? Because the branch [anaph] of his majesty, his splendor, his crown, his radiance, and his brilliance covers all the chambers of Arabot of the uppermost firmament, like the Creator of the world. Just as of the Uppermost Creator it is written: "His majesty covered the heavens, and the earth was full of His praise," so too does Anaphiel Y. the Prince cover with his majesty and splendor all the chambers of the uppermost Arabot.
18.7: And Anaphiel Y. the Prince, when he sees Kotertashiel Y. the great, awesome, and honored Prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Kotertashiel? Because he is appointed in authority over the four headwaters of the River of Fire beneath the Throne of Glory. And every prince from whom a voice goes out and who enters before the Shekhinah only goes out and enters by his permission, forasmuch as the walls of the four headwaters of the River of Fire are entrusted to his hand. Moreover, the height of his stature is seventy thousand myriads of parasangs, and he is the crown of fire of the River of Fire, and he goes out and enters before the Shekhinah to declare the merit of all who come into the world, as it is said: "The judgment was set, and the books were opened."
18.8: And Kotertashiel Y. the Prince, when he sees Sheked-Hazaya Y. the great, mighty, awesome, and honored Prince, would remove the crown of glory from atop his head and fall upon his face. And why is his name called Sheked-Hazaya? Because he weighs [shokel] all merits in the scale-pan before the Holy One, Blessed be He. And Sheked-Hazaya Y. the Prince, when he sees Zephanurya Y. the great, mighty, awesome, honored, and majestic Prince, who is revered by all the heavenly host, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is his name called Zephanurya? Because he breathes with it in pur[ity] [ … in] the River of Fire, and his dais is in its place. And this Patriel the Prince, when he sees Hanukkah Y. the great, zealous, radiant, honored, majestic, wonderful, exalted, standing, and revered Prince among the princes—they are the great ones who reveal the secrets of the Throne of Glory—he removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face. And why is his name called Hanukkah Y. Y. the Prince? Because he girds himself with beams of life and wraps himself in a cloak of life, to stand and to come before the righteous of the world and the pious of the world, so that they might live through them the life of the world. And Hanukkah Y. Y. the Prince, when he sees the six great, numerous, and honored princes who stand higher than he, removes the crown of glory from atop his head and falls upon his face.
18.9: And these are the names of the six princes: Sophriel Y. the Slayer, the great, honored, majestic, pure, ancient, and mighty Prince; and Sophriel Y. the Giver of Life, the great, mighty, honored, majestic, pure, ancient, and mighty Prince. And why is his name called Sophriel Y. the Slayer? Because he is appointed over the books of the dead; for everyone whose day of death has arrived, he writes him in the books of the dead. And why is his name called Sophriel Y. the Giver of Life? Because he is appointed over the books of the living; for everyone whom the Holy One, blessed be He, desires for life, he writes him in the books of the living by the authority of the Omnipresent.
18.10: And lest you say: "Since the Holy One, blessed be He, sits upon His throne, they too sit and write?" Does it not say: "And all the host of heaven standing by Him"? "The host of heaven" is not said, but rather "and all the host of heaven," which teaches that even the great princes, whose like does not exist in the heights of heaven, do not perform the needs of the Shekhinah except while they are standing. And how do they write while they are standing? Rather, this one stands upon the wheels of the whirlwind, and that one stands upon the wheels of the storm; this one is clothed in a royal robe, and that one is clothed in a royal robe; this one is wrapped in a cloak of majesty, and that one is wrapped in a cloak of majesty; this one is bound with a royal bond, and that one is bound with a royal bond; this one is enveloped in a garment of brilliance, and that one is enveloped in a full garment of brilliance; this one’s appearance is like the appearance of lightning And this one’s appearance is like the appearance of lightnings; this one shines like the sun in its strength, and this one’s hue is like the herb in its growth. And this one’s radiance is like the radiance of the Throne of Glory, and that one’s radiance is like the radiance of the Throne of Glory. This one’s height is as the height of seven heavens, and that one’s height is as the height of seven heavens. This one’s wings are as the days of the year, and this one’s wings are as the days of the year.
18.11: This one’s wings are as the breadths of the firmament, and that one’s wings are as the breadths of the firmament. This one’s lips are like the gates of the East, and that one’s lips are like the gates of the East. This one’s tongue is as the height of the waves of the sea, and that one’s tongue is as the height of the waves of the sea. From this one’s mouth issues a flame, and from that one’s mouth issues a flame. From this one’s mouth issue lightnings, and from that one’s mouth issue lightnings. This one, from his touch fire burns, and that one, from his touch fire burns. From this one’s tongue burns a torch of fire, and from that one’s tongue burns a torch of fire. This one, upon his head is a sapphire stone, and that one, upon his head is a sapphire stone. This one, upon his shoulders is a Kerukel-wheel, and that one, upon his shoulders is a Kerukel-wheel. This one, in his hand is a scoop of burning coal, and that one, in his hand is a scoop of burning coal. This one, in his hand is a cloud of flame, and that one, in his hand is a cloud of flame. The measure of the scoop is three thousand myriads of parasangs, and the measure of the cloud of flame is three thousand myriads of parasangs. The measure of each and every letter that they write is three hundred and sixty-five parasangs.

19.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, the Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them—the prince over these six great princes—there is one prince, a leader and honored, mighty and majestic, feared and revered, valiant and strong, great and magnified, powerful and glorified, wonderful and exalted, pure and beloved, ruler and handsome, and a minister and sublime, such that there is none like him among all the princes together: Rikbiel Y., the Great and Terrible Prince is his name, for he stands beside the Chariot. And why is his name called Rikbiel? Because he is appointed over the wheels of the Chariot, and the legs of the Chariot are entrusted into his hand. And how many are the wheels? Eight, two; six for each and every direction, and around them four winds surround them. And these are the winds: the wind of the gale, the wind of the tempest, the wind of might, and the wind of the earthquake. And from beneath them, four rivers of fire pull and go out, one river for each and every side, and between them are surrounded and standing four Four clouds, and these are they: clouds of fire, clouds of torch, clouds of burning coal, and clouds of lightning. These clouds are set and stand opposite their four legs, and the legs of the Living Creatures (Chayyot) are placed upon their legs. And there is a noise like the noise between wheel and wheel, and a noise like the noise between wheel and wheel.
19.2: And when the time arrives to utter song, the multitude of wheels roar, the multitude of their host trembles; all the captains and taskmasters roar, all the horsemen recoil, all the mighty ones are shaken, all the hosts and all the troops are hurried, all the appointed ones are dismayed, all the princes and the soldiers faint, all the ministers are convulsed, and all the angels and the standards. And the sound of service passes from wheel to wheel, from cherub to cherub, from living creature to living creature, from ophan to ophan, from seraph to seraph: "Extol Him who rides upon the clouds, by His name Yah, and exult before Him."

20.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel of the Lord, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is one prince, great and powerful, and Chayyel-YHWH is his name—a majestic and awesome prince, a surpassing and mighty prince, a great and awesome prince; a prince at whose presence all the sons of the heights are shaken, for he is able to swallow the entire world at once. And why is his name called Chayyel-YHWH the Prince? Because he is appointed over the Living Creatures (Chayyot), and he strikes the Living Creatures with whips of light, and he adorns them with pure gold, praise, and thanksgiving, and he hastens them to say after "Holy": "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place."

21.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: There are four Living Creatures corresponding to the four winds; every single Living Creature is as the fullness of the entire world. And each and every one has four faces, and every single face is like the face of the East. And each and every one has four wings, and every single wing is like the covering of the world. And each one has faces within faces, and each and every one has wings within wings. The measure of the faces is two hundred and forty-eight faces, and the measure of the wings is three hundred and sixty-five wings. And upon the head of each and every one are bound two thousand crowns, and every single crown is like a rainbow in the cloud; its radiance is like the radiance of the orb of the sun, and the beauty of each and every one is like the radiance of the planet Venus. In a vision,

22.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is one prince, noble and wondrous, strong and praised with every kind of praise; Kerubiel-YHWH is his name. He is a mighty prince, full of the power of might; a prince of beauty, and beauty is with him; a righteous prince, and righteousness is with him; a holy prince, and holiness is with him; a prince glorified by thousands of hosts; a prince who exalts himself amidst myriads of myriads of armies. At [the sound] of the quaking and the agitation, the turmoil and the trembling of the … camps, the foundations travail in dread and the Aravot quake from their counsel.
22.2: The height of his stature is full of burning coals; the height of his stature is as the height of the seven heavens, the breadth of his stature as the breadth of the seven heavens, and the thickness of his stature as the thickness of the seven heavens. The opening of his mouth is a burning torch, and his tongue is a consuming fire; his eyes are like the radiance of lightning, and his eyes are like sparks of brilliance. The appearance of his face is like a burning fire, and a crown of holiness is upon his head, upon which the Explicit Name is engraved, and from which lightnings go forth.
22.3: The bow of the Shekhinah is between his shoulders, his sword is like lightning upon his loin, and his arrow is like lightning upon his belt; coals of consuming fire are upon his neck, and coals of broom-wood are all around him. And behold, the splendor of the Shekhinah is upon his face, rays of majesty are upon his wheels, and a royal turban is upon his crown. His whole body is full of eyes, and the height of his stature is [full] of wings. From his right a flame blazes, and from his left a flare flashes; burning coals issue from his body, torches go out from him, and lightnings flash from his face. With him there is always quaking and quaking, and always quaking within quaking. Two princes of the Chariot are in his place.
22.4: And why is his name called Kerubiel-YHWH the Prince? Because he is appointed over the chariot of the Cherubim, and the Cherubim of Might are delivered into his hand. With the crowns of his head he is glorified, and with the diadem of his pate he is adorned. He sings the praise of their form; he hastens the beauty of their hue; he increases the abundance of their wisdom; he magnifies the joy of their preciousness; he sings the song of their praise; he recites the strength of their beauty; he brightens the radiance of their glory; he beautifies the splendor of the grace of their kindnesses; he fashions the desire of their dwelling; he embellishes the compassion of their beauty; he glorifies the truth of their majesty; and he exalts the [secret] of their praise. to prepare a seat for the One who dwells among the Cherubim; and the Cherubim stand beside the Holy Creatures, their wings at the height of their heads, the Shekhinah upon their backs, the splendor of glory upon their faces, a song of praise within their mouths, their hands beneath their wings, and their feet covered by their wings. A horn of majesty is upon their heads, the radiance of the Shekhinah is upon their countenances, and the Shekhinah is upon their backs. Sapphire stones are around them, pillars of fire are upon their four sides, and pillars of torches are at their sides—one sapphire on this side and one sapphire on that side. There are Creatures of sapphires and Creatures of broom-wood; one Cherub on this side and one Cherub on that side, and the wings of the Cherubim overshadow one another upon their crowns in glory, spread out to sing with them a song to the Dweller of the Skies, and to revere with them the beauty of the King of Kings.
22.5: And Kerubiel-YHWH is his name, the Prince who is appointed over them; he arranges them in fair and beautiful orders, and he extols them with every kind of precious and honorable adornment, glorifying them with honor and strength to perform the will of their Maker at every moment; for above the height of their heads there is always great glory, the King who dwells among the Cherubim.

23.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: How many winds blow from beneath the wings of the Cherubim? There blows a hovering wind, as it is said: "And the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters." There blows a strong wind, as it is said: "And the Lord drove the sea with a strong east wind." There blows an east wind, as it is said: "And the east wind carried the locusts." There blows a wind of snows, as it is said: "And a stormy wind He made; the Lord is a counselor of peace." There blows a wind of jealousy, as it is said: "And a spirit of jealousy passed over him." There blows a wind of earthquake, as it is said: "And after the wind an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake." There blows the wind of the Lord, as it is said: "And we went out by the spirit of the Lord, and He set me down." There blows an evil wind, as it is said: "And the evil spirit departed from him." There blows a wind of wisdom, and a wind of understanding, and a wind of knowledge, and a wind of the fear of the Lord, as it is said: "And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him: a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and might, a spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord." There blows a wind of rains, as it is said: "The north wind brings forth rain." There blows a wind of lightnings, as it is said: "lightnings … "
23.2: For rain, He brings out the wind from His treasuries.  [which shatters] rocks, as it is said: "The Lord shattered with a great and strong wind."  that restores water, as it is said: "And God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided." from across the wilderness, and it struck the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men. destroys among these winds; for a "stormy wind" is nothing other than the wind of Satan. And all these winds have no dwelling place except beneath the wings of the Cherubim, as it is said: "And He rode upon a cherub and flew; and He was seen upon the wings of the wind." And to where do these winds go and terminate? This teaches that they emerge from beneath the wings of the Cherubim and fall into the sphere of the sun, as it is said: "It goes toward the south and turns toward the north; round and round goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns." And from the sphere of the sun they return and fall into the rivers and the seas, upon the mountains and the hills, as it is said: "For behold, He who forms mountains and creates the wind." And from the mountains and hills they return and fall into the seas and the rivers. And from the seas and rivers they return and fall upon the inhabited world, and from the inhabited world they return and fall upon the towns and the provinces.
23.3: And from the towns and provinces they return and fall into the Garden, and from them they return and fall into Eden, as it is said: "walking in the garden at the breeze of the day." And within the Garden of Eden they are pleasant and blow from this side to that; and they are perfumed by the spices of the Garden and the ointments of Eden until they are infused and filled with the spirit of pure fragrance, and they bring the scent of the ointments of the Garden and the spices of Eden before the righteous and the pious, the heirs of the Garden of Eden and the Tree of Life in the time to come, as it is said: "Awake, O north wind, and come, O south wind! Blow upon my garden, let its spices flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden and eat its choice fruits."

24.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Glory of the height, how many chariots does the Holy One, blessed be He, have? He has chariots of Cherubim, as it is said: "And He rode upon a cherub and flew." He has chariots of wind, as it is said: "And He was seen upon the wings of the wind." He has chariots of a swift cloud, as it is said: as it is said: “Behold, the Lord rides upon a swift cloud.” He has chariots of clouds, as it is said: “Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud.” He has chariots of the altar, as it is said: “I saw the Lord standing upon the altar.” He has chariots of myriads, as it is said: “The chariots of God are myriads, thousands upon thousands.” He has chariots of the Tent, as it is said: “And the Lord appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud.” He has chariots of the Tent of Meeting, as it is said: “And the Lord spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting.” He has chariots of the Mercy Seat, as it is said: “And he heard the voice speaking to him from above the Mercy Seat.” He has chariots of sapphire stone, as it is said: “And under His feet was like a work of sapphire brickwork.” He has chariots of princes, as it is said: “And I bore you on eagles’ wings”; and “princes” are none other than those who endure and are as princes. He has chariots of the shout, as it is said: “God has gone up with a shout.” He has chariots of the highest heavens, as it is said: “Extol Him who rides upon the highest heavens.”
24.2: He has chariots of thick clouds, as it is said: “Who makes the thick clouds His chariot.” He has chariots of living beings, as it is said of the Living Creatures that they “ran and returned,” running by permission and returning by permission, for the Shekhinah is over the top of their heads. He has chariots of the wheelwork, as it is said: “And He spoke to the one among the wheelwork.” He has chariots of a swift cherub, for He rides upon a swift cherub; and in the hour that He rides upon a swift cherub and flies upon one of its feet, and before He has even set down its second foot, He surveys eighteen thousand worlds in a single glance, and understands and sees in all of them, and knows each and every one of them, until He sets down its second foot upon [the ground], as it is said: “The circumference shall be eighteen thousand.” And even as He surveys all these, He surveys every single day, as it is said: “From heaven the Lord looks down upon the children of men to see if there is any who understands, seeking God.” He has chariots of wheels, as it is said: “And the wheels were full all around.” He has chariots of His holy throne, as it is said: “God sits upon His holy throne.” He has chariots of the Throne of Yah, as the interpretation of: “A hand upon the throne of Yah.” He has chariots of the throne of judgment, as it is said: “And the Lord stands up for judgment.”
24.3: He has chariots of the Throne of Glory, as it is said: “A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, the place of our sanctuary.” He has chariots of a high throne, as it is said: “And I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up.”

25.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is a prince, great and awesome, mighty and honored, a leader and chief, ancient and strong—Apaphnos is his name, who has sixteen faces, four faces for each and every side, and four faces for each and every side; a hundred wings for each and every side, and a hundred wings for each and every side. And he has eight thousand seven hundred and sixty-six eyes, corresponding to the [hours of the] days of the year; six thousand one hundred and ninety-one and sixteen for each and every side, and six thousand one hundred and ninety-one and sixteen for each and every side. And as for those two eyes in his face, from each and every one lightnings flash, and from each and every one torches burn, and no creature is able to look at them, for anyone who looks at them is immediately burned. And the height of his stature is a journey of six thousand five hundred years, such that no eye can see and no mouth can speak of the power of the might of his strength, except for [the word] “How great!” alone.
25.2: And why is his name called Apaphnos? Because he is appointed over the Ofanim [Wheels], and the Ofanim are delivered into his hand, and he is appointed to serve the Ofanim. He stands over them every single day and serves and glorifies them, and exalts and arranges their course, and polishes their splendor, and refines their dwelling, and inclines their faces, and anoints their seat. And he rises early and stays late over them night and day, to increase their glory, and to enlarge their beauty, and to make them swift in the praise of their Holy One. And the Ofanim are all full of eyes and all full of wings, seven [wings] corresponding to wings, and wings corresponding to six, and their wings shine like the brilliance of a radiant light. And seventy-two sapphire stones are fixed upon their garment on the right of each and every one, and seventy-two sapphire stones are fixed upon their garment on the left of each and every one, and four emerald stones are fixed fixed upon the crown of each and every one, whose radiance goes forth to the four winds of Arabot, and upon all of them, whose radiance goes forth to the four winds of the world. And why is its name called bareqet? Because its radiance is like the appearance of lightning [baraq]. And they are surrounded by booths of radiance, booths of splendor, booths of light, sapphire, and bareqet, because of the appearance of the likeness of the Shekhinah. And the likeness of their entrance …

26.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above them there is a prince, wondrous and mighty, great in honor, powerful and formidable, a leader and a noble, a ready scribe, glorious and honored and pleasant. He is entirely full of praise and brightness, entirely full of splendor, entirely full of light, entirely full of beauty, entirely full of loveliness, and entirely full of greatness and majesty. His likeness is like the angels, and his body like the Seraphim, and his radiance like the lightnings, his form like torches, and his beauty like sparks, and his majesty like rivers, his glory like electrum. His body is like a bright light; his appearance is like the great appearance, gleaming like the seven heavens; and the light of his eyelids is like the sevenfold light; and a sapphire stone is upon his head, as large as the whole world, like the radiance of the very heavens for purity.
26.2: And his body is full of eyes like the stars of heaven, which are beyond searching and beyond numbering; and every single eye is like the planet Venus, and some of them are like the lesser luminary, and some of them are like the greater luminary. From his ankles to his knees they are like stars of lightning; and from his knees to his thighs like the planet Venus; and from his thighs to his loins like the light of the moon; from his loins to his neck like the light of the sun; and from his neck to the crown of his head like a light that cannot be measured.
26.3: And the crown upon his head is like the radiance of the Throne of Glory; the size of the crown is a journey of five hundred years. And there is no kind of radiance, and no kind of brilliance, and no kind of brightness, and no kind of light in the world that is not fixed in that crown. And that prince, Seraphiel YHWH is his name. And the crown on his head, "Prince of Peace" is its name. And why is his name called Seraphiel YHWH? Because he is appointed over the Seraphim, and the Seraphim of flame are delivered into his hand. And he stands over them night and day, and teaches them song, praise, beauty, strength, and majesty, to glorify their King.
26.4: Every single day [they offer] praise and holiness. And how many are the Seraphim? Four. [They have] four wings [corresponding to] the four winds of the world. And how many wings do they have? Six; six wings corresponding to the six days of Creation. And how many faces do they have? Sixteen faces—four faces for each wind. And the measurement of the Seraphim and the spirit of each and every one corresponds to the seven heavens. The measurement of the wings—each and every wing is like the fullness of a heaven. Their marble-whiteness is of a beat, and every single beat corresponds to the East; and each and every one shines like the appearance of the Throne of Glory. Even the Holy Living Creatures, the Wheels of Majesty, and the Cherubim of Splendor cannot look upon it, for whoever looks upon it, his eyes grow dim from the great radiance that is upon it.
26.5: And why is their name called Seraphim? Because they burn (sorfim) the ledgers of Satan. Every single day, Satan sits with Samael, the prince of Rome, and with Dubiel, the prince of Persia, and writes the iniquities of Israel upon ledgers. They give them to the Seraphim to bring them before the Holy One, blessed be He, to destroy Israel from the world. But the Seraphim know the secrets of the Holy One, blessed be He—that He does not wish for this nation of Israel to fall. What do the Seraphim do? Every single day, they take them from the hand of Satan and burn them in a consuming fire that is opposite the high and exalted Throne, so that they might not come before the Holy One, blessed be He, at the hour when He sits upon the Throne of Judgment and judges the whole world in truth.

27.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above the Seraphim there is one prince, more excellent than all the princes, more wondrous than all the ministers; Deganiel-YHVH is his name. He is appointed over the treasuries of books, and he brings out and brings in the caskets of writings and the Book of Remembrance written before the Holy One, blessed be He. He recognizes the seals of the caskets, and he opens and takes the books and gives them into the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He. And the Holy One, blessed be He, takes them from his hand and places them before Him, before the scribes, to read in the Great Court, for on the day of the eve of the Heavenly Household. And why is his name called Deganiel? Because every single word and the word that went forth from Him, from it was an angel created; and he stands in the service of the ministering angels and utters song before the Holy One, blessed be He, at the hour when the time arrives to say "Holy."

28.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Above all these there are four great princes, Watchers (Shirin) and Holy Ones (Kadishin) are their names. [They are] exalted and honored, awesome and pleasant, wondrous and mighty, and greater than all the children of the heights. There are none like them among all the princes of the heights, and none of their standing among all the ministers, for each and every one is equal to them all. Their station is opposite the Throne of Glory, and their standing is before the Holy One, blessed be He. For the radiance of their station is like the radiance of the Throne of Glory, and the splendor of their form is like the splendor of the Shekhinah. They are glorified by the glory of the Might and praised by the praise of the Shekhinah. Furthermore, the Holy One, blessed be He, does nothing in His world until He consults with them first, and afterward He acts, as it is said: "The matter is by the decree of the Watchers (Irin), and the request by the word of the Holy Ones (Kadishin)" [Dan. 4:14]. There are six Watchers and six Holy Ones. And how do they stand before the Holy One, blessed be He? It teaches that one Watcher stands on this side and one Holy One stands on this side; one Watcher stands on this side and one Holy One stands on this side. And forever they raise up and they cast down nations to the earth, and they raise up the lowly to the heights.
28.2: And every single day, when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits upon the Throne of Judgment and judges the whole world, and the books of the living and the books of the dead are opened before Him, all the children of the heights stand before Him in awe and fear, in dread and trembling. At that hour, the Holy One, blessed be He, sits in judgment upon the Throne of Judgment; His garment is white like snow, and the hair of His head is like pure wool, and His cloak is entirely like a shining light, and He is completely full of righteousness like a breastplate. And these Watchers (Shirin) and Holy Ones (Kadishin) stand before Him like officers before the judge, and they deliberate upon each and every matter, and they conclude the matter that comes before the Holy One, blessed be He, according to the law, as it is said: "The matter is by the decree of the Watchers (Irin), and the request by the word of the Holy Ones (Kadishin)." Some of them decide the law and the matters, and some of them decree the decrees in the Great Court that is in Arabot. Some of them ask the questions before the Might, some of them They conclude the matters corresponding to that which is above them; they conclude and descend and fulfill the decrees on the earth below, as it is said: “Behold, a Watcher and a Holy One came down from heaven; he cried aloud with might” [Dan. 4:10–11].
28.3: And so it says: “The matter is by the decree of the Watchers, and the request by the word of the Holy Ones” [Dan. 4:14]; and by the judgment, the beast was passed away from under it, and they stripped the leaves from the branch. And why are they called Watchers (Irin) and Holy Ones (Kadishin)? [They are called] Shirin because they sanctify the body and the soul with tongs of fire on the third day of judgment, as it is said: “After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, that we may live before Him” [Hos. 6:2].

29.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Each and every one of them has seventy names, corresponding to the seventy languages that are in the world, and all of them are after the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And every single name is written with a pen of flame upon the awesome crown that is upon the head of the High and Exalted King. And from each and every name, sparks and lightnings issue forth; and from each and every one, a horn of light. They are surrounded by white brilliances from each and every one; and from each and every one, a star of light and canopies of radiance surround them, so that even the Seraphim, the Holy Creatures, and the wheels of the throne-base in the seventy heights are unable to gaze upon them.

30.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Whenever the Great Court sits in the heights of Arabot of the firmament, it is not opened to any creature in the world, except for those great princes who are called by the name of the Lord (YHVH), after the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. And how many are these princes? Seventy-two princes of the kingdoms in the world, besides the Prince of the World, who speaks in praise of the world before the Holy One, blessed be He, every single day when they open the book of the deeds of the world that are written therein, as it is said: “The court sat in judgment, and the books were opened” [Dan. 7:10].

31.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: At the hour when the Holy One, blessed be He, sits upon the Throne of Judgment, Righteousness stands at His right, and Lovingkindness at His left, and Truth before His face. And at the hour when a wicked man comes before Him for judgment, the measure of Lovingkindness goes forth toward his face, as if to mitigate and protect him; immediately the man falls upon his face, and all the angels of … are afraid and tremble. the angels of destruction to His right, according to the matter that is said: “And a throne shall be established in mercy, and he shall sit upon it in truth” [Isa. 16:5].

32.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: When this House is opened, [and] the Book—half of which is fire and half of which is flame—[those who] issue forth from before Him at every single moment to execute judgment upon the wicked; and His sword is enkindled from the chain, its brilliance flashing like lightning, traversing from one end of the world to the other, as it is said: “For by fire will the Lord contend” [Isa. 66:16]. And all who inhabit the world are afraid and tremble before Him; from before Him His messengers, and sparks and flashes are enkindled like lightning from one end of the world to the other, and sparks and flashes issue from it as numerous as the stars of the firmament, according to the matter that is said: “A fire goes before Him and burns up” [Ps. 97:3].

33.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: At the hour when the Holy One sits upon the Throne of Judgment, the angels of mercy stand at His right, the angels of peace stand at His left, and the angels of destruction stand before Him. One scribe is above Him, and one Cherub is above Him, and the Seraphim of glory surround the four directions of the Throne like walls—walls of lightnings; and the Ofannim surround, and they are like torches around the Throne of Glory; and a brilliance of fire and a cloud of torchlight encompass them from the right and from the left. And the Holy Creatures carry the Throne of Glory from beneath them, each and every one with three fingers; and for each and every one, the three fingers—the measure of the height of their fingers—each one is eight thousand and seven hundred, sixty and eight thousand parsas.
33.2: And from beneath the feet of the Holy Creatures, seven rivers of fire pull and issue forth; and each and every river, its breadth is three hundred and sixty-five thousand parsas, and its depth is two hundred and seventy and forty and eight thousand myriads of parsas, and their course is without limit and without number. And each and every one turns like a kind of dome in the four directions of the Arabot of the firmament, and falls, all of it, downward from Ma'on to Zebul, and from Zebul to Shehaqim, and from Shehaqim to Raqia, and from Raqia to Shamayim, and from Shamayim upon the tumult of the wicked, as it is written: “Behold, the storm of the Lord has gone forth in fury, a whirling tempest; it shall whirl down upon the head of the wicked” [Jer. 23:19].

34.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: The hooves of the feet of the Holy Creatures are surrounded by seven clouds of glory. Before the clouds of glory they are surrounded by seven walls of flame. Before the walls of flame they are surrounded by seven walls of torches. Before the walls of torches they are surrounded by seven walls of hailstones. And before the hailstones they are surrounded by stones of hail. And before the stones of hail they are surrounded by stones of the wings of the storm. And before the stones of the wings of the storm they are surrounded by sparks of flame. And before the sparks of flame they are surrounded by storm clouds. And before the storm clouds they are surrounded by fire and mercy. And before the fire and mercy they are surrounded by those who say "Holy." And before those who say "Holy" they are surrounded by those who say "Blessed." And before those who say "Blessed" they are surrounded by mists of purity. And before the mists of purity they are surrounded by the wheels of the Chariot. And before the wheels of the Chariot they are surrounded by a thousand camps of fire and myriads of hosts of flame. And between camp and camp and between host and host, a mist is set between them so that they do not burn from the fire.

35.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron, the Angel, Prince of the Presence, said to me: Four hundred and ninety-eight thousand myriads of camps has the Holy One, blessed be He, in the height of the Aravot of the firmament. And every single camp has four hundred and eighty-six thousand angels. And every single angel—the height of his stature is like the Great Sea, and the appearance of his likeness is like the appearance of lightning, and their eyes are like torches of fire, and his arms and his feet are like the appearance of burnished bronze, and the roar of the sound of their words is like the sound of a multitude. And all of them stand before the Throne of Glory in four rows, and the princes of the army stand at the head of every single row. There are those among them who say "Holy," and there are those among them who say "Blessed," and there are those among them who run on missions, and there are those among them who stand in service, as it is stated: "Thousands upon thousands served Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him; the judgment was set, and the books were opened" [Dan. 7:10]. And at the hour when they stand to say "Holy" at the beginning, a storm wind issues from before the Holy One and ascends into the camp of the Shekhinah, and there is a great storm among them, as it is said: "Behold, the storm of the Lord has gone forth in fury, a whirling storm" [Jer. 23:19].
35.2: At that hour, thousands upon thousands Halphan: of them are twenty thousand sparks of [every] type; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of torches; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of whispers; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of flames; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of males; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of clouds; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of spirits; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of burning fire; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of flame; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of m sparkles; twenty of them are a thousand thousands of hashmalli of light, until they take upon themselves the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven. And the One who bears and creates them all [does so] in dread, in fear, in trembling, and in quaking, in commotion, and in anguish, in dread, and in quivering. And afterward He returns them to their first measure, so that the fear of their King may be before them at every hour, in order that they may direct their hearts to say a song at every hour, as it is said: "And one called to another and said: Holy."

36.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: In the hour when the ministering angels seek to say a song, the River of Fire rises up with many thousand thousands and myriads of myriads of the power of the mights of fire, and it flows and passes from beneath the Throne of Glory between the camps of the ministering angels and the troops of sh Aravot. And all the ministering angels descend first into the River of Fire and immerse themselves in the fire of the River of Fire, and they immerse their tongues and their mouths seven times in the River of Fire. And afterward they ascend and put on garments of the folds of the loins, and wrap themselves in adornments of hashmal, and stand in four rows facing the Throne of Glory in every single firmament.

37.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: In the seven palaces stand four chariots of the Shekhinah, and before each and every one stand four camps of the Shekhinah. Between camp and camp flows and passes a river of fire, and between river and river they are surrounded by mists of purity. And between each one, pillars of nefritz stand and are revealed. And between pillar and pillar, wheels of flame surround and stand. And between wheel and wheel, sparks of a torch surround. And between spark and spark, treasuries of lightnings surround. And the treasuries of lightnings are surrounded by wings of the storm. And behind the wings of the storm, the storehouses of the tempest surround, and behind the storehouses Storms encompass [them], winds upon winds, voices upon voices, thunders upon thunders, sparks upon sparks, quakings upon quakings.

38.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: In the hour when the ministering angels say “Holy,” all the pillars of the firmaments and their wings are shaken, and the gates of the palaces of the firmament of Aravot are moved. The foundations of the world and the skies are shaken, and the chambers of Ma’on and the chambers of Makhon are convulsed. All the orders of the firmament—the constellations and the stars—are dismayed, and the disk of the sun and the disk of the moon are hurried and flee from their paths, running backward twelve thousand parasangs. And they seek to throw themselves down from heaven because of the thunder of the voice of their melody and the noise of their majesty, and the sparks and lightnings that go forth from their mouths, as it is said: “The voice of Your thunder was in the whirlwind, the lightnings lit up [the world],” etc., until the Prince of the World calls to them and says to them: “Be silent in your places and do not fear, for the ministering angels are singing a song before the Holy One, blessed be He,” as it is said: “When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”

39.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: When the ministering angels say “Holy,” all the Explicit Names that are engraved with a pen of flame upon the Throne of Glory take flight and fly with sixteen wings, and they encompass and surround the Holy One, blessed be He, in the four directions of the place of the glory of His Shekhinah. And the angels of the host, the ministers of flame, the Ophannim of power, the Cherubim of the Shekhinah, the Holy Creatures, the Seraphim, the Erellim, the Taphsarim, and all the legions of fire, and the devouring legions, and the ranks of torches, and the hosts of flame, and the holy princes—bound with crowns, clothed in royalty, wrapped in glory, [wearing] ephods of splendor, gathered in robes, girded with majesty—fall upon their faces three times and say: “Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.”

40.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: In the hour when the ministering angels say “Holy,” one opening comes, [and] the ministers of His throne and the attendants of His glory go out in great joy from beneath the Throne of Glory; and each and every one [has] in their hands presents and rewards and many myriads of crowns of stars, of ivory, [with] the appearance of the luster of the star Venus, and they bind them to the ministering angels.
40.2: [angels] of the service and the great princes, those who say “Holy” three times: one [group] that says “Holy,” one for the sake of saying “Holy, Holy,” and one for the sake of saying “Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord of Hosts.” And at the time when they do not say “Holy” [at the proper time], a consuming fire goes forth from before the little finger of the Holy One, blessed be He, and falls into their ranks and is divided into four hundred and ninety-six thousand [portions], corresponding to the four camps of ministering angels, and devours them all at once, as it is said: “A fire shall go before Him and set on fire His enemies round about” (Ps. 97:3). Afterward, the Holy One, blessed be He, opens His mouth and speaks one word and creates others in their stead, like seventy new ones; and each and every one stands in song before the Throne of Glory and says “Holy,” as it is said: “They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness” (Lam. 3:23).

41.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: Come and I will show you the letters with which heaven and earth were created; the letters with which seas and rivers were created; the letters with which mountains and hills were created; the letters with which trees and grasses were created; the letters with which stars and constellations, the cycles of the moon, the disk of the sun, the planets, Pleiades, and all kinds of luminaries of the firmament were created; the letters with which ministering angels were created; the letters with which Seraphim and Holy Creatures were created; the letters with which the Throne of Glory and the wheels of the Chariot were created; the letters with which the necessities of the world were created; the letters with which wisdom and understanding, knowledge and discernment, humility and uprightness—by which the whole world is sustained—were created. And I went with him, and he took me by my hand and raised me up on his wings and showed me all those letters, which are engraved with a pen of flame upon the Throne of Glory, and sparks and lightnings go forth from them and cover all the chambers of Aravot.

42.1: Rabbi Ishmael said: Metatron said to me: Come and I will show you where the waters are suspended in the highest heights, and where fire burns within hailstones, and where lightnings flash within mountains of snow, and where thunders roar in the heights of the supreme, and where flame shall blaze within parching fire, and where voices make themselves heard in thunder.
42.2: And I spread [my wings] and went beside him, and I took hold of his hand, and he raised me up on his wings and showed me all of them. And I saw water suspended in the heights of the Arabot firmament by the name of Yah, Ehyeh Asher Ehyeh; and their fruits descend as rain and saturate the face of the world, as it is said: “From the fruit of Your works the earth is satisfied” (Ps. 104:13). And I saw fire and snow and hailstones that are enfolded one within another, yet they do not cause harm, by the name of “Consuming Fire,” as it is said: “For the Lord your God is a consuming fire,” etc. (Deut. 4:24). And I saw lightnings that flash within mountains of snow, yet they are not damaged, by the name of Yah, the Lord, the Rock of Ages, as it is said: “For in Yah, the Lord, is the Rock of Ages” (Isa. 26:4). And I saw thunders and voices that roar within flames of fire, yet they are not damaged, by the name of El Shaddai Rabbah, as it is said: “I am El Shaddai” (Gen. 17:1). And I saw blaze and flame that blaze and flame within a burning fire, yet they are not damaged, by the name of Yah upon the throne of Yah, as it is said: “And he said: Because a hand is upon the throne of Yah” (Ex. 17:16). And I saw rivers of fire within rivers of water, and rivers of water within rivers of fire, yet they are not damaged, by the name of “He who makes peace,” as it is said: “He makes peace in His heights” (Job 25:2), for He makes peace between fire and water, between hail and fire, between wind and cloud, and between sparks and sparks.
